definition: In this historical philosophical usage, objective reference means considering an idea in relation to the fact or object it is about, rather than merely as a private mental state. In that sense, the idea is գնահատed by how far it answers to truth or certainty.

provenance.revision: 1901 New York Macmillan original; archive index checked 2026-10-18
provenance.scope: Source record Opinion (in philosophy); pinned source text

reasons: The packet does not state (or clearly imply) that “objective reference” is contrasted specifically with “private mental state.” It only says that “objective reference” concerns how ideas are taken in relation to a “standard of truth or certainty” and gives “value or function of ideas taken in their objective reference.”

The definition’s first sentence (“considering an idea in relation to the fact or object it is about”) is not directly supported by the packet’s wording; the packet does not describe objective reference in those terms, beyond the general phrase “standard of truth or certainty.”
